title: Associate Director, Pipeline and External Innovation Communications
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Overview:
The Associate Director, Pipeline and External Innovation Communications, plays a key role in driving strategic science and data communications across AbbVie’s R&D pipeline, with primary responsibility for certain Immunology programs and additional support for other therapeutic areas and cross-therapeutic area (cross-TA) initiatives. The role partners closely with the Immunology and broader TA communications leads to articulate and amplify AbbVie’s innovation narrative, translate complex science into compelling stories, and ensure coordinated communications around key pipeline milestones, informed by regular engagement with Asset Strategy Teams (ASTs) and active tracking of program progress. The role also supports external innovation communications, including strategic alliances, research collaborations, licensing agreements, and other business development activities. The Associate Director will report to the Head of Pipeline and External Innovation Communications and work cross-functionally with key stakeholders across R&D, Corporate Affairs, and Commercial.
Key Responsibilities:
Lead or support communications planning and execution for scientific data disclosures, including medical congress presentations and publications, as well as clinical development milestones, regulatory filings, and pre-commercial announcements.
Serve as a communications partner to relevant Asset Strategy Teams (ASTs), attending meetings and maintaining ongoing visibility into program progress, decisions, risks, timelines, and near- and long-term milestones.
Translate AST and program updates into proactive communications plans, stakeholder recommendations, milestone readiness, and external engagement opportunities.
Provide flexible cross-TA communications support for enterprise priorities, emerging pipeline needs, and high-impact milestones, working in close collaboration with TA pipeline communications leads.
Collaborate cross-functionally with R&D, Clinical, Medical Affairs, Commercial, Regulatory, Alliance Management, and Corporate Affairs partners to ensure aligned and integrated communications.
Support communications related to external innovation, including strategic partnerships, research collaborations, licensing agreements, and other business development activities, with an emphasis on Immunology and relevant cross-TA opportunities.
Work in close partnership with Media Relations, Social Media, Internal Communications, and other channel teams to develop and deploy integrated communications strategies across external and internal channels.
Contribute to enterprise-wide non-branded initiatives, including disease awareness, scientific thought leadership, platform and capability storytelling, and cross-portfolio narratives.
Develop and track communications KPIs to measure impact, refine strategies, and demonstrate the value of Immunology and cross-TA pipeline communications to internal stakeholders.
Foster a collaborative, cross-functional mindset and help cultivate a culture of rigorous, audience-centered scientific storytelling within the Corporate Affairs organization.
Education and E xperience:
Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree or background in life sciences strongly preferred.
7-10 years of experience in integrated communications, with a focus on scientific, data, R&D, or pipeline communications in the healthcare or biopharmaceutical industry.
Solid understanding of the drug development lifecycle and the broader life sciences industry; familiarity with Immunology disease areas, scientific platforms, and competitive dynamics is preferred.
Strong understanding of new and emerging communications trends
Demonstrated ability to translate complex scientific data into clear, compelling narratives tailored to diverse audiences.
Proven track record of high-quality tactical execution and measurable outcomes.
Ability to provide strategic communications counsel to senior leaders and cross-functional partners while flexing across broader enterprise priorities.
Strong project management skills, with the ability to prioritize and lead multiple initiatives in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.
Excellent verbal, written, and visual storytelling skills.
Collaborative, proactive, and solutions-oriented mindset.
Comfortable navigating ambiguity, with strong business acumen and enterprise thinking.
Core Competencies
Scientific and strategic fluency and the ability to learn across therapeutic areas
Business storytelling and audience-centric messaging
Cross-functional and cross-TA collaboration and influence
Innovation and continuous improvement
Accountability and operational excellence
Enterprise-first mindset and flexibility across priorities

The Regional MOSL advances field scientific strategies.
Serve as the Medical lead within the integrated account team for assigned accounts, playing an integral role in appropriate planning, strategy development and execution.
Participate across assigned therapeutic area and healthcare landscape strategic committees.
Customized communication of scientific, health outcomes, and health policy information to HCDMs and influencers.  Document and communicate meaningful observations that lead to Scientific Intelligence on a regular basis; Identify emerging scientific, health economic, and health policy trends and integrate gaps and learnings into functional strategy and objectives.
Primary interface and initial point of contact for small-scale, RWE opportunities with regional level HCDMs.
Anticipate, identify and address population-level scientific, outcomes research, and health policy needs of customers serving as the trusted advisor to the customer.  Leverage internal and external resources to meet customer needs.
Facilitate scientific exchange, as necessary, between AbbVie Medical Leadership, including Medical Affairs, TA Medical Directors, and HEOR with accounts to support internal and external customer objectives.
Maintain and continually enhance clinical, scientific, and healthcare landscape expertise.  Participate in various therapeutic advisory activities involving both marketed and investigational products, spanning the full product life-cycle.
Engage regional healthcare decision makers in compliant, peer level scientific exchange integrating clinical evidence, health economics and outcomes research, and real-world evidence.
Territory includes:  (PA, DE, WV, MI, IN, OH, KY) - applicant must live in the territory to be considered
Advanced scientific degree required (Pharm.D., M.D., D.O., Ph.D., or equivalent)
The position requires extensive experience in Managed Care, healthcare consulting, pharmaceutical industry, medical affairs or related environment.
Completion of relevant residency or fellowship programs may be considered in lieu of some work experience.
Account management experience preferred.
Advanced scientific and business acumen. Includes sophisticated understanding of the healthcare landscape.
Demonstrates excellent leadership, executive presence, and presentation skills.
Advanced innovative problem solving, critical thinking, and communication skills.
Self-motivated and solution oriented.
Advanced ability to network and collaborate effectively across multiple levels within an organization.
Competencies
Uses disease state and standard of care expertise to support credible outcomes-focused scientific exchange with healthcare decision makers.
Applies understanding of patient and caregiver experience, including access barriers and care delivery realities, to scientific discussions.
Applies product knowledge across AbbVie and therapeutic landscape portfolios, including clinical, outcomes, and real-world evidence, to contextualize value and access discussions.
Interprets regulatory, policy, and access landscape considerations to support compliant engagement and inform regional planning.
Defines and communicates holistic value propositions by integrating clinical, economic, and humanistic evidence relevant to regional healthcare decision making.
Uses appropriate evidence sources, including real-world evidence and health economics data, to support outcomes-focused dialogue.
Translates regional Scientific Intelligence into actionable input that informs medical planning, evidence needs, and access strategies.
Applies strategic thinking to align scientific engagement with regional objectives, account priorities, and healthcare system needs.
Engages in effective, two-way scientific communication to build trusted relationships with healthcare decision makers.
Collaborates across cross-functional partners and the In-Field Team (IFT) to support aligned execution and Scientific Intelligence.

Regional healthcare access decision makers (HCDMs) and influencers

AbbVie Analytical Research & Development (Analytical R&D) is a global analytical scientific organization responsible for all CMC analytical activities related to the development of AbbVie's pharmaceutical products.  Our scope includes AbbVie's diverse pipeline of innovative small molecule medicines and spans from the selection of Discovery candidate molecules to Late Stage Clinical.  We are building a world-class team of scientists and leaders who will drive the advancement of industry-leading analytical capabilities and make meaningful contributions to advance AbbVie's pipeline of innovative medicines.  Careers in AbbVie Analytical R&D provide unique opportunities to work with global and cross-functional teams to drive exceptional science and innovative product development strategies.  We are looking for diverse candidates with strong scientific experience to join the AbbVie Analytical R&D team and can offer exciting and rewarding career opportunities for these candidates.
Position Description:
This Senior Scientist – Solid State Characterization position will be in a technical specialty group - Physical Analytical Chemistry (PAC) withing Analytical R&D.  The PAC group is a global team of experienced and innovative scientists which utilize a diverse set of physical analytical tools to advance CMC development programs by providing insights and driving the understanding of materials, processes, and products.  Additionally, the group contributes to development and justification of control strategies and authors relevant sections of regulatory submissions across all development phases.
We are looking for a subject matter expert in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of drug substances (DS) and drug products (DP), from early form discovery through regulatory filing. The role focuses on single crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), electron diffraction (3D ED/MicroED), Rietveld refinement, quantitative phase analysis (QPA), and phase-appropriate polymorph quantitation methods both in drug substance and drug products. The scientist will work closely with Molecular Profiling Drug Development, Process Chemistry, Formulation, Process Engineering, Analytical, Operations, Quality Assurance and CMC-Regulatory.
Key Responsibilities:
Support new product development with advanced methods development and validations, technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements.

Serve as the PXRD expert for supporting solid form screening, identification, crystallinity, and stability studies; perform indexing, Pawley/Le Bail fitting, Rietveld refinement, and structure determination from powder data.
Perform quantitative phase analysis: Quantify polymorphic and amorphous content in DS and DP using Rietveld, whole-pattern, and multivariate approaches, addressing low drug load, excipient interference, preferred orientation, and micro absorption.
Apply advanced diffraction such as VT/VH-XRPD, in situ, synchrotron, and PDF analysis to study phase transformations and poorly crystalline/amorphous materials.
Apply SCXRD and 3D ED/MicroED structure determination, including absolute configuration and crystal packing of APIs, salts, cocrystals, hydrates, and solvates; generate calculated powder patterns and CIF reports.
Conduct orthogonal solid-state characterization including X-ray diffraction, thermal analysis, moisture sorption, microscopy, spectroscopy as applicable for solid form, impurity and stability studies
Support solid form control strategies per ICH Q6A, author Module 3 sections and health authority responses, and ensure GMP and data integrity compliance.
Highly autonomous and productive in performing laboratory work, method development and troubleshoot; processing, interpreting, and visualizing data to facilitate project team decisions
Represent PAC on CMC teams, lead form-change investigations, mentor scientists, and implement new diffraction technologies.
Build strong relationships with peers and cross functionally with partners outside of team to enable higher performance.

Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding code of conduct, safety, appropriate handling of materials, controlled drug and radioactive compounds, and GxP compliance, where applicable.
Qualifications:
Bachelors, Masters, or Ph.D. in Chemistry, Material Science, Physics, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related field typically with minimum 10 (BS), 8 (MS), or 0 – 2 (Ph.D.) years related industry experience.
Strong technical background in solid state characterization, excellent analytical problem-solving, communication, presentation, and cross-functional collaboration skills. Capable of independently developing and troubleshoot analytical methods.
Extensive hands-on PXRD experience, including indexing, Rietveld refinement, QPA, and polymorph and amorphous quantitation.
Track record of developing and validating PXRD methods for DS and DP in a GMP environment, with knowledge of ICH Q2(R2), Q6A, Q14, and USP .
Expertise in small molecule SCXRD structure solution and refinement, including disorder modeling and absolute structure; and knowledge of 3D ED/MicroED approaches.
Proficiency with tools such as Olex2, SHELX, CrysAlisPro, TOPAS, Diffrac Eva and DQuant, GSAS-II, HighScore, Mercury, and the CSD.
Hands-on experience with DSC, TGA, hot-stage and polarized light microscopy, DVS, and strong data analysis and interpretation skills.
Experience with Raman/FTIR/NIR, solid-state NMR, SEM, SAXS, micro-CT, and crystal structure prediction, and particle characterization is preferred.
Experience with AI/ML and data science for automation of phase identification and Rietveld/QPA workflows, chemometrics, and Python or R scripting is preferred.
Experience with biophysical characterization tools of nanoDSC, DLS, SEC-MALS, CD, AUC, nanoDSF in peptide, LNP and biologic materials, formulations and process characterization is preferred.
Strong pharmaceutical industry experience in solid state characterization is preferred
Ability to coordinate activities and work simultaneously on multiple projects, in a global, fast-paced setting where priorities may change quickly.
High attention to detail and creative problem solving while exhibiting strong interpersonal skills and proven ability to work independently as well as part of cross functional teams
Knowledge of instrument set-up, troubleshooting, management and maintenance.
Experience extracting insights from multidimensional data sets, along with other physical analytical characterizations, and connecting to pharmaceutical materials, processes, and products
Practical knowledge of organic structure, functional groups, chemistry, and modern spectroscopic techniques as applied to small-molecule analytical analysis.
Create a learning environment, open to suggestions and experimentation for improvement.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Partner Integrations
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:
The Partner Integration team is responsible for integrating new business partners and functionality into Airbnb’s product. We work to improve both the supply and demand side of Airbnb’s Stays, Experiences and Services businesses through thoughtfully designed product experiences for Guest and Hosts.
We recently launched exciting new features such as grocery delivery and airport transfers, as well as integrations with smart lock providers, rewards programs and more. We are looking to rapidly expand our offerings.
You will be working closely with a strong, fast-moving team integrating new product functionality into the Guest experience of Airbnb’s core product. This role also interacts with a large cross-functional team of partners across product and design, business and partnerships, customer support and more
The Difference You Will Make:
As an Engineer on the Partner Integrations team, you will:
Contribute directly to company growth in new areas as we explore partnerships outside of Airbnb.
Lead projects end-to-end – from working with partners directly, to clicking that launch button.
Identify patterns that allow us to scale new partnerships quickly in the future.
Have attention to detail about the user experience.
A Typical Day:
Design, write and test new APIs and integrations with partners.
Write documents to propose, align and document changes to the system.
Debug external integrations and join the team on-call rotation.
Collaborate with cross-functional partners such as Product, Program, Design and Engineers, and directly with external partners.
Provide input in team roadmap and technical direction.
Build large scale backend solutions that are efficient, reliable, performant and scalable.
Your Expertise:
6+ years of experience
Experience designing scalable and resilient large-scale service-oriented architectures
Experience leading projects
Previous experience working with third party API’s is a plus.
Previous experience with authentication or secure signing mechanisms is a plus.
Passionate about reliability, efficiency, availability, and system quality.
Good judgment in making and communicating tradeoffs to balance short-term business needs with long-term technical quality.
High sense of user empathy and the ability to identify and solve for user needs and friction.
End-to-end mentality that transcends team boundaries and helps find globally optimal solutions.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to work well within a team and with teams across the engineering organization.

title: Embedded Software Engineer, Platform
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

The Embedded Platform team owns the on-device software that ensures Base’s fleet of Linux-class hardware runs workloads reliably and securely, APIs for interacting with devices individually and at scale, and the telemetry stack that provides visibility at both the device and fleet level. As an embedded software engineer on the team, you’ll own complex, mission-critical systems on our fleet of devices end to end: bootloaders, secure boot, kernel drivers, networking, telemetry storage and offload, application data streams, and more.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Design, build, and ship reliable, performant, and secure SDKs that control and monitor Base’s batteries across our fleet of Linux-class hardware.

 - Own platform software end to end across the full stack: bootloaders and secure boot, networking, kernel and device drivers, and build systems.

 - Build scalable tracing infrastructure that collects core dumps, logs, and diagnostics across our compute platforms and moves them reliably to cloud-based log ingest and indexing backends.

 - Ship the device-side features of Base’s in-house fleet management platform: device telemetry, remote configuration, and safe OS and firmware rollouts.

 - Investigate hard problems down to the root cause, from first principles, and borrow ideas from adjacent fields like cloud and distributed systems when they offer a better answer.

Channel.

declarations.
 Ensure compliance with U.S. export requirements, destination-country import
regulations, applicable trade laws, sanctions and restricted-party requirements, and
company policies.

recordkeeping, and regulatory compliance.

compliance requirements.
 Support tariff and export classification, country of origin determinations, and trade

compliance due diligence and transaction reviews, and support audits and
investigations.

 Identify process improvement and automation opportunities and support

• Customs compliance
• Import/export operations
• IMMEX program administration

manufacturing industry.

 Knowledge of USMCA and other free trade agreement requirements.

• U.S. Export Compliance

 Bachelor's degree in engineering, international trade, customs administration, supply

Sustain and improve existing manufacturing lines: Provide daily engineering support for existing in-house manufacturing lines.
Own and drive continuous improvement of mechanical fixture s and processes to improve product quality, throughput, and cost. Utilize objective data and statistical analysis to inform and drive decisions.
Ideate, prototype, and implement simple, robust mechanical fixture s and tooling designed to error-proof complex assembly steps, take operator skill levels and manual technique out of the equation, and maximize production repeatability.
Lead root cause investigations and drive dispositions for assembly-related defects using Product and Process FMEAs as guidance.
Support quality system compliance including ECO review and implementation, discrepant material dispositions, nonconformance evaluations, and quality notifications.
Troubleshoot, resolve, and document equipment and process malfunctions in compliance with GXP and Intuitive Quality System requirements.

Lead Design Verification and Validation (V&V) builds
Coordinate cut-in/implementation in production.
Provide manufacturing feedback for supplier change requests (SCRs).
Support equipment and process qualification efforts (IQOQPQ and PPQs)

Specify and refine BOMs, workflows/travelers, and detailed work instructions.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams (e.g. Production, Design Engineering, Quality Engineering, Supplier Engineering, Project Management) to meet project objectives including Design Verification & Validation and product launch. Create and revise manufacturing-related risk documents including Process FMEAs, Manufacturing Line Specifications, Equipment Specifications.
Leadership Responsibilities: Leads/participates in continuous improvement initiatives focused on material cost reduction, capacity enhancement, and streamlining continuity of material supply.
Mentors and sets project tasks for Manufacturing Engineers on their specific project team, and on other teams as needed, to further company expertise & effectiveness.

Keep the organization’s vision and values at the forefront of decision-making and action.

Integration with standard equipment: Hands-on experience developing custom tooling designed for integration into standard manufacturing equipment (e.g., presses, crimpers, heat stakers, ultrasonic welders).
Strong mechanical aptitude and fundamentals: Deep knowledge of mechanical design principles, fabrication methods, precise material selection, and surface treatments to optimize tooling performance.

Foundation in design, fabrication, and assembly process development for complex mechanical assemblies.
Demonstrated understanding of component manufacturing processes such as injection molding, transfer molding, thermoforming, machining, stamping, and MIM.
Technical problem-solving skills with ability to identify root cause and drive corrective action (Fishbone, 8D Analysis)
Ability to employ statistical methods (Cpk, ANOVA, Design of Experiments) in data analysis for process development and problem-solving.
Effective communication skills (verbal, written, and presentation) and comfortable interacting with production technicians, product design engineers, planning, buyers, clinical engineers, and suppliers.
Able to travel periodically to suppliers or Intuitive manufacturing sites.

Minimum B.S. Mechanical Engineering or related technical discipline. M.S. preferred.
8+ years with a B.S or 6+ years with an M.S of experience as a process or manufacturing engineer supporting products with significant mechanical content.
Working Conditions
Abhility to lift, maneuver, and troubleshoot fixture s and tools
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience in mid-volume manufacturing of single-use devices or complex electro- mechanical assemblies is a plus.
Experience in medical device design controls and manufacturing (ISO 13485) is a plus.
Machine tool experience is a plus.

Build alignment across Customer Service, Finance, Supply Chain, Regulatory, Quality, and IT.

title: Principal HVDC Engineer, Grid Integration Engineering
description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.
Invenergy follows a hybrid schedule, working in office Monday through Thursday and remotely on Fridays if work permits.
This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.
Job Description
Role Scope and Interface
This role leads study scopes, technical reviews, issue resolution, and cross-functional coordination within Grid Integration Engineering. Interconnection & Grid Analysis retains formal submissions, process management, and agreement negotiations. OEMs and consultants execute contracted studies; Grid Modeling supports modeling and validation consistent with project-phase responsibilities. Engineering and Construction retain detailed implementation and field execution.
Responsibilities
HVDC Interconnection and GBX Cluster Studies
•    Lead the technical scope and coordination of HVDC interconnection studies with SPP’s Transmission Working Group (TWG), MISO, and AECI, including related affected-system studies and material modification assessments.
•    Manage GBX generation cluster studies, coordinating project and OEM data, model packages, study assumptions, consultant deliverables, technical comments, and dependencies with the HVDC interconnection workstreams.
•    Develop study scopes, case lists, schedules, and technical deliverables; manage consultants and coordinate inputs with the HVDC OEM, Interconnection & Grid Analysis, Grid Modeling, and project teams.
•    Oversee model sourcing, quality testing, validation, and cross-platform benchmarking. Maintain consistency of PSS/E and PSCAD models, plant configurations, control settings, and data across interconnection and OEM studies.
•    Review power flow, short-circuit, dynamic stability, and electromagnetic transient (EMT) results; resolve model deficiencies and study findings, and assess proposed mitigations with Interconnection & Grid Analysis and Engineering.
•    Translate final study outcomes and agreement obligations into the Design Basis for Grid Compliance and final interconnection-study model package, including accepted material modifications, for handoff to Engineering and Grid Modeling.
OEM System Design and Performance Verification
•    Lead Invenergy’s technical oversight of OEM system design studies, including main circuit parameters, equipment ratings, transient stress, insulation coordination, harmonics, and AC/DC system interactions.

title: Retail Sales Manager - Roswell (GA)
description:
Job Description:
Job Description:
The Mars Retail Sales Manager is responsible for executing Mars Sales Strategy by applying fact-based selling techniques to influence customer decisions and achieve goals and objectives at Store Level.  Key responsibilities include delivering the Perfect Store, executing Account Headquarter plans, and delivering seasonal sell thru objectives and company priorities by identifying incremental selling opportunities for categories under your responsibility.
The primary role of the Retail Sales Manager (RSM) is to leverage data and insights to sell and execute company strategies and priorities by achieving Sales KPI objectives and creating best in class in-store conditions to engage consumers and drive consumption.  The expectation is that RSM will command strong knowledge of the category, shopper trends and consumer usage occasions, enabling them to effectively sell incremental assortment and in-store solutions.
As an entry point into our MARS Sales organization, RSM is responsible for building strong customer relationships and collaborating across the Sales functions to identify and resolve operational issues.
The position requires a high degree of integrity with the ability to work efficiently and effectively in an independent fashion without direct supervision.  This position is field based within a defined geography and reports directly to a Retail Sales Lead.
Key Responsibilities
Build and maintain long-term, trusted relationships with customers by demonstrating strong consultative selling skills to drive sales, retailer profit, ROI, and market share.
Create value by delivering customized sales presentation(s) based on retailer opportunities and priorities to sell incremental orders and mutually beneficial in-store solutions.
Monitor and analyze performance metrics to identify and execute solutions to achieve territory and region KPIs, retailer category growth, and account/company business targets.
Leverage data and demonstrate a strong priority setting to deliver channel/retailer specific seasonal and limited time offer to sell through targets.
Serve as a primary point of contact for customers, ensuring clear communication of sales priorities, orders, and promotional plans.
Position yourself to be a trusted expert, asking open-ended questions and tailoring solutions to specific needs.
Influence merchandising and operational resources to ensure instore excellence, compliance with execution standards, and timely implementation of sales initiatives.  These include assortment priorities (core and innovation), shelving objectives and planogram integrity, as well as incremental semi-permanent and temporary displays.
Responsible and trusted use of technology is essential, including accurate data entry, analysis of sales data to build a selling story, and effective utilization of company systems to support decision-making and performance tracking.
May have Compression call responsibilities. Comfortable preparing and selling to Market Managers, District Mangers depending on customer base of your territory.
Direct 3rd party providers (where applicable) for in-store execution (including seasonal surge).
Where applicable, sell throughout the year by providing business updates to the store's decision maker and contracts which will support delivery of the distribution, shelving, and display objectives.  Enforce compliance.
Maintain high on shelf availability by working with KDM to address inventory discrepancies and order fulfillment.
Participate in team conference calls, training, and attend all sales meetings.
Responsible for storage facility and managing product rotation, inventory allocation, supplies, etc., in an efficient and effective way.

This role is an individual contributor.
This role interfaces with customers at store level
This role has a reasonable impact on sales organizations and a reasonable impact on the company.

Bachelor’s Degree
Knowledge/Experience
Minimum Qualifications :
A bachelor’s degree, or HS Diploma and equivalent work experience
Demonstrated proficiency with intermediate technology tools, including mobile devices and basic business applications.
Strong analytical, problem solving, and negotiation skills.
Excellent interpersonal, communication, and relationship building capabilities.
Ability to lift and carry up to 40lbs
Able to sit, stand and/or drive for long periods of time, as well as frequently bend, kneel and stoop
Ability to walk for a minimum of 6 ½ hours per day
Demonstrate ability to work remotely
Subject to outside weather conditions and changing climates
Must live within territory boundaries
Ability to travel overnight if required
Work scheduled may include early mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays based on business needs.
Role requires daily travel to multiple customer locations and a valid driver’s license with a clean driving record.
Preferred Qualifications:
A bachelor’s degree and significant experience in field sales and territory management
2+ years with at least one year of selling experience
Proven ability to influence customers through professional selling skills and data driven insights.
Experience using technology to analyze performance, manage accounts, and support sales execution.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Work, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Power Bi.
Prior Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) and/or retail sales experience
Prior selling experience in convenience, grocery or Walmart channels.

We are looking for a  Cloud Solution Architect – Cloud & AI Data Platform  with deep knowledge in data platforms and analytics to support customers in building secure, scalable, and AI-ready solutions on Microsoft Azure.
In this customer-facing role, you’ll guide organizations through their data modernization and AI journeys—leading architectural design sessions, proof-of-concept initiatives, and production deployments for mission-critical workloads. Your focus will be on ensuring performance, resiliency, and security across solutions that drive measurable business value.
As a key member of the Cloud & AI Data Platform team, you’ll use established repeatable IP and execution frameworks to deliver high-quality outcomes and accelerate solution adoption. You’ll work with cutting-edge technologies such as  Microsoft Fabric ,  Azure Databricks ,  Cosmos DB , and  Purview , helping unlock the full value of their data and AI investments.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees, we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Business Impact: Operates according to required operational excellence and proven practice standards throughout all sales stages/activities/tools of record (e.g., pipeline updates, time tracking) with minimal guidance from more experienced peers. Collaborates across Microsoft and customer/partner teams through on-strategy delivery with minimal guidance from more experienced peers to achieve customer/partner objectives and increase/partner customer satisfaction. Contributes to managing business and technical risks, adapting methodology and applying governance principles to identify, communicate, and minimize business and technical risks. Executes work in compliance with industry and Microsoft guidelines and procedures. With minimal guidance from more experienced peers, prioritizes among competing demands in their work and identifies where impact occurs with customers, ensuring alignment with business priorities and goals.
Contributes to the identification, escalation, and mitigation of blockers using appropriate tools and processes to accelerate solution deployment, value realization and usage/consumption with minimal guidance. Continues to develop business, technical, industry, and/or enterprise knowledge and applies it to architecture or support projects with minimal guidance from more experienced peers to help meet business and information technology (IT) requirements and resolve identified constraints.
Identifies new opportunities for Consumption, Usage & Unified expansion (especially Enhanced Solutions) at scale with minimal guidance from more experienced peers based on business value to customer/partner and clear understanding of the Microsoft value proposition for supported platforms to empower cloud success, foster and strengthen security and resiliency, and drive AI innovation. Actively listens to and respectfully challenges customers/partners, building trust to then advocate for alternative architectures/solutions/approaches that shape and/or enhance customer requirements with minimal guidance from more experienced peers. Contributes to the identification and evaluation of industry trends (e.g., customer industry verticals, information technology [IT] industry), gathering of customer/partner insights (e.g., feedback around technical preferences, environments, business needs, competitive landscape), and mapping of existing architecture and digital transformation solutions to customer/partner business outcomes. Proactively captures opportunities in appropriate systems, processes, and tools, working collaboratively across the organization to execute on opportunities aligned with Microsoft's Customer Engagement Model.
Delivers solutions in line with company methodologies (e.g., product offerings such as value-based deliverables [VBDs], advice, training, technical validation) with minimal guidance from more experienced peers, ensuring proven practices and patterns are followed to prepare customers for operational readiness and achievement of their business goals. Leveraging knowledge of change management proven practices, and/or involving the change management team, contributes to helping the customer deploy for long-term organizational adoption to increase customer satisfaction and drive consumption/usage. Guides customers/partners towards a well-architected (e.g., secure, resilient, artificial intelligence [AI]-enabled), and cost- and performance-optimized solution with minimal guidance from more experienced peers to increase retention and expansion opportunities. Contributes to providing feedback to Unified Delivery Team on VBDs to refine and further develop content.

Learns and develops an understanding of customer goals, and contributes to the definition of customer/partner conditions of success. Addresses customer/partner dissatisfaction with minimal guidance, and may contribute to the execution of strategies to improve customer experience, value realization, and acceleration of transformation.

Contributes to the identification of patterns across customers/partners/territories/industries and leveraging them to develop strategic and actionable insights. May present business cases to program managers, with minimal guidance, to influence product roadmaps, decision-making, bug fix prioritization, and own and drive initiatives as appropriate.

title: Critical Environment Technician Manager
description:
Overview
In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day and we need you as a Data Center Critical Environment Technician Manager.
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I CE Technician Manager, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development for all employees and offers trainings and growth opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion trainings and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.
Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture
Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
May travel up to 25%, typically domestically for training and/or supporting another site. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed and promotes a safe working culture to empower less experienced team members. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance
Prepares and submits highly complex reports as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates, or using ad hoc methods required to support trending and analysis (e.g., Root Cause Analysis [RCA] reports) and may review prior reports delivered by less experienced team members. Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for highly complex and/or interdependent equipment and disciplines to ensure safe and reliable execution. Reviews completed work using approved tools and procedural templates from less experienced technicians for accuracy and completeness. Provides assignment and completion oversight of team members for mandatory, technical, and procedural training material. Assigns and oversees procedure development and reporting to team members. Analyzes findings from reports and documents observations.
Guides, oversees, and performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs for multiple disciplines and multiple equipment types of increasing complexity with no supervision, while serving as a subject matter expert for one discipline - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Provides consultation to colleagues on maintenance and repairs through deep understanding of equipment, systems and their interrelations. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Oversees everyday, complex, large-scale tasks for a single discipline or equipment across disciplines. Ensures follow up action items are addressed in a timely manner. Masters the maintenance of all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance across all disciplines and supports team members with subject matter expertise. Plans, coordinates, and presents maintenance items for review and approval in their area of responsibility.
Provides and/or assigns team members to provide necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site for all procedure levels of risk (LOR). May take part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Engages to address and resolve circumstances when supplier/vendor work has been stopped to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates and/or assigns team members to coordinate across all LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Coordinates and schedules supplier/vendor on-site activities. Coordinates with vendor to schedule maintenance and determines availability of equipment/parts, as directed. Resolves or escalates observed vendor quality issues. Reviews and approves vendor supplier field service reports, invoices, and work orders.
Processes method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Leads and provides guidance on coordinating activities and establishing associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities. Advises engineer partners or project management colleagues on project scope process or execution methodology. Presents for review and approval MSOW in their area of responsibility.
Acts as a subject matter expert, performing troubleshooting independently for multiple equipment, systems, subsystems, and component types. Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Determines when troubleshooting efforts are deemed adequate and communicates or escalates to suppliers, engineers, or more experienced colleagues as needed. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment in all disciplines work and how to troubleshoot to subsystem level. Provides consultation to less experienced colleagues with troubleshooting systems and problems. Ensures troubleshooting completion paths are escalated appropriately and successfully by their team members. Oversees and advises their team members on troubleshooting systems and/or investigates root causes.
Equipment and Systems Operations
Takes part in, and oversees team in the inspection and supervision of critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds regularly for unsafe or abnormal conditions to develop and analyze trends. Understands critical system alarms for multiple discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) and understands risks or impacts to other subsystems across the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify all alarms. Uses technical expertise, prior experience, and device analytics to recognize trends with equipment behavior and checks potential issues as they arise. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems. Ensures all monitoring equipment repair, replacement, and maintenance work meets or exceeds Microsoft Service Level Agreement (SLA) requirements. Uses data trends to develop or produce predictive analyses of equipment performance.
Works on complex, advanced tasks (e.g., stabilization, resolution, recovery) independently. Serves as an operations specialist in a major area of operations (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls, generators) and provides oversight and training/mentorship to team members on tasks regarding these subsystems. Demonstrates an understanding of and operates equipment and systems across all disciplines (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls) with knowledge of the interactions between them and overall operation of a data center. Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
Safely and quickly responds to and leads an onsite incident response team for all abnormal conditions that impact operations, and coordinates with other critical facilities professionals to perform corrective repairs, without supervision. Gathers necessary information and creates incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies and contacts/engages appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur, and collects or provides appropriate escalation details or context to support incident management requirements. Develops new or follows preexisting emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Directly provides and leads and coordinates emergency monitoring response plans for irregular or malfunctioning conditions. Oversees team during emergency incident management, assigning tasks for corrective repair as appropriate. Communicates directly to leadership, advises the business on the current conditions, safety concerns, and next steps for incident mitigation and/or resolution. Oversees incident detection, analysis, and containment efforts. Serves as technical expert in ensuring emergency operating procedures (EOPs) are consistent with proper incident response.
Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks utilization and time tracking results for team members, within applicable task management systems. Reviews and validates added required data, documents, changes logged, and procedures upkeep details (related to building management systems and reports) conducted by team members. Guides and coaches team in CMMS usage best practices. Audits and reviews team's data to ensure performance adherence to assigned work tasks. Generates reporting from CMMS for outstanding and ongoing work orders. Generates ad hoc or custom CMMS reports as needed for management. Reviews spare equipment and parts, updates stock, and signal stock replenishment with suppliers and/or coordination with Materials Handling partners.
People Management
Managers deliver success through empowerment and accountability by modeling, coaching, and caring. Model: Live our culture. Embody our values. Practice our leadership principles. Coach: Define team objectives and outcomes. Enable success across boundaries. Help the team adapt and learn. Care: Attract and retain great people. Know each individual’s capabilities and aspirations. Invest in the growth of others.
Other
Embody our culture and values
Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications
High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent.
5+ years mission critical services work/applied learning experience (e.g., high availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or related fields) OR equivalent experience.
Background Check Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
Microsoft Cloud Background Check:  This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
Citizenship Verification:  This position requires verification of citizenship due to citizenship-based legal restrictions. Specifically, this position supports United States federal, state, and/or local  government agency customers and is subject to certain citizenship-based restrictions where required or permitted by applicable law. To meet this legal requirement, and as a condition of employment, the successful candidate’s citizenship will be verified with a valid passport.
This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Candidates must have authorization to work in the United States that does not now or in the future require employer sponsorship.
Preferred qualifications
1+ year(s) experience in a specialized area (e.g., mechanical field, electrical field, controls field) or related field.
Associate's Degree or technical trade certification (e.g., military, trade school), or higher-equivalent education AND 7+ years mission-critical services experience (e.g., high-availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or related fields) OR High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent AND 10+ years mission critical services experience (e.g., high-availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or related fields) OR equivalent experience.
1+ year(s) people management experience.

Own the end-to-end execution of complex Volume Licensing deals , partnering across sales, deal desk, partner, operations, credit, invoicing, and trade teams to enable accurate, timely, and compliant revenue processing.

Improve deal quality and velocity through structured deal reviews, escalation management, post-close analysis, and field guidance that reduce errors, late submissions, exceptions, and avoidable processing bottlenecks.
Build trusted partnerships across the field and operations ecosystem, guiding stakeholders to the right resources, increasing self-service and pre-validation adoption, and supporting the successful rollout of new commerce processes and capabilities.
Drive continuous improvement and AI-enabled transformation across Quote-to-Cash workflows, combining human expertise with AI automation to improve quality, speed, scale, and customer outcomes—advancing Microsoft’s Frontier Firm vision.
Escalation & Issue Resolution — Act as a key escalation contact, coordinating with sellers, partners, and PDMs to resolve issues efficiently and hold the line on proper escalation paths.

Deep field and partner knowledge, understanding of the Microsoft sales process, or similar industry experience.

Ability to multi-task and project manage many tasks simultaneously, working under continual deadline constraints.
Ability to simplify complex situations and apply analytical and problem-solving skills.

title: Research Intern - Quantum Applications
description:
Overview
Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment.
Researchers in quantum applications are designing the algorithms, software, and workflows that will make fault-tolerant quantum computers useful for solving real-world problems in chemistry, materials science, and physics.
Microsoft's deep investments in the field are advancing the state of the art in quantum algorithms, resource estimation, and hybrid quantum-classical workflows, with applications designed alongside the hardware that will run them. In addition, the company's researchers take a rigorous, realistic view of where quantum computers will outperform classical methods and what resources each application will require. The research, tools, and software that result from this investment are built into the Microsoft Quantum Development Kit (QDK) and shared with the broader scientific community through open-source releases such as QDK/Chemistry to accelerate discovery and help solve some of humankind's most challenging problems.
Responsibilities
Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer.
The Research Intern will explore chemistry and physics applications for early fault-tolerant quantum computers, contributing to the development and evaluation of algorithms and workflows that leverage emerging quantum capabilities, in combination with machine learning and/or AI. Potential research directions include:
Quantum algorithms and simulation:  Develop and analyze algorithms for quantum dynamics and complex quantum systems, including Hamiltonian simulation, and study their error and computational resource requirements.
Quantum computing for chemistry and materials:  Develop computational methods, including downfolding techniques, that map complex chemical and materials problems onto efficient representations suitable for quantum simulation.
Machine learning and quantum systems:  Investigate how quantum computing and machine learning can be used together to simulate complex quantum systems, this includes exploring the limits of neural networks in capturing and learning many-body quantum complexity, to understand where quantum computers provide a true advantage.
Working closely with researchers and engineers, the Research Intern will develop new algorithmic techniques and workflows, perform theoretical and numerical analysis, and assess their potential for scientifically meaningful applications on fault tolerant quantum computers.

description:

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and advancing toward AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world environments. Working across the full model and systems stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the physical constraints of real-world systems to improve people’s lives.

About the Role

As a Mechanical Design Engineer on the Robotics team, you’ll design battery packs for robots and help define how those packs integrate into the rest of the system. In this hands-on individual contributor role, you’ll own mechanical designs from early architecture and packaging through prototyping, validation, and production. You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Enjoy owning mechanical designs and staying hands-on through builds, testing, and debugging.

title: Model Policy Manager, Emerging AI Misuse
description:
About the Team

The Model Policy team within OpenAI’s Safety Systems organization defines how increasingly capable AI models should behave in real-world settings. We turn research on emerging risks into model behavior policies, evaluations, and safeguards.

About the Role

As AI systems become more capable, the same advances that expand their legitimate uses can also lower barriers to harm. Emerging misuse risks range from AI assistance with conventional weapons development and the misuse of AI-enabled robotics to fraud, impersonation, and other forms of abuse that people can carry out at scale using AI agents. You’ll build threat models for how people could misuse AI in digital and physical settings, assess what access to AI changes in practice, and use that evidence to define how models should respond.

This role is based in San Francisco. We offer relocation support and work from the office three days a week, with optional work from home on Thursdays and Fridays.

In this role, you will: 

 - Build and update threat models as capabilities evolve. Assess what people could plausibly do, what expertise and resources they would need, and how AI changes those barriers.

 - Define when models should help, limit assistance, or refuse in situations where the same capability has legitimate and harmful uses.

 - Turn expert safety judgment into instructions, training examples, and evaluations that teach models when to help, when to limit assistance, and when to refuse.

 - Turn threat models into evaluation scenarios and grading guidance. Analyze model outputs, red-team findings, and deployment data to identify where models enable misuse or block legitimate work.

 - Partner with research, engineering, security, and product teams to apply findings to model training, deployment decisions, and monitoring.

You might thrive in this role if you: 

 - Have hands-on experience building, testing, or assessing dual-use technologies, or a track record of threat modeling grounded in how people use and misuse real systems.

 - Demonstrate deep practical experience in one relevant domain and the judgment to know when to bring in experts from others.

 - Are able to assess whether a capability demonstrated in a test materially changes what someone could do outside it.

 - Can translate technical evidence and uncertainty into clear policy boundaries and measurable evaluation criteria.

 - Have experience analyzing gold sets, evaluation results, and training data to spot inconsistent human labels, assess how annotator disagreement affects measured performance, and decide what to investigate next.

 - Are comfortable working hands-on with model data and evaluation results, including inspecting examples, analyzing failure patterns, assessing data quality, and distinguishing policy failures from grader, model, or system failures.

 - Use empirical evidence to develop and refine safety policies and safeguards.

 - Work well across disciplines and revises their judgment as capabilities and evidence change.

 - Enjoy fast-paced, collaborative research environments where priorities shift as models, evidence, and risks change.

title: Researcher, Cyber Safety Training
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Safety Research at OpenAI is responsible for ensuring our most capable models can be safely deployed in the real world. The Safety Training team develops the research and engineering methods that shape model behavior through post-training, reinforcement learning, evaluation, and deployment feedback.

Our work focuses on making models helpful, reliable, and aligned with safety policies across model types, modalities, and product surfaces. We work across both longer-term safety research and the core post-training work needed to improve production models.




ABOUT THE ROLE

You’ll work directly on the large training runs that shape OpenAI’s frontier models. Your focus will be teaching models to help people do legitimate security work while recognizing when their assistance could enable harm. A model that refuses to help a defender investigate a security issue can fail in a different way from one that helps someone misuse it. You’ll study both kinds of mistakes and use what you learn to improve the next training run.

We’re looking for someone with hands-on machine learning experience who wants to bring security judgment into model training. You might come from cybersecurity and want to go deeper on post-training, or from reinforcement learning and want to build substantial expertise in cybersecurity.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Work with cybersecurity researchers to identify situations where context changes what help a model should give.

 - Design complex and realistic cyber safety evaluations.

 - Research post-training techniques that robustly improves the cyber safety of the frontier models.

 - Work with the core post-training team to bring promising methods into large model runs and verify that the safety improvements hold at scale.

 - Coordinate and collaborate with cross-functional teams, including T&S, legal, policy and other research teams, to ensure that our products meet the highest safety standards.
   
   


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - Have trained or fine-tuned models yourself and can describe an experiment where you used the results to change how you trained the next model.

 - Bring practical security judgment from industry work, a research project, collaboration with a security team, or capture-the-flag competitions. We also welcome reinforcement learning practitioners motivated to develop that judgment alongside security researchers.

 - Can build and debug the code behind a training experiment, from preparing data to checking whether a change in the results reflects a real change in model behavior.

 - Enjoy working through ambiguous cases with domain experts and translating what you learn into concrete decisions about how a model should respond.

description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. Role Summary Rivian is seeking a Senior Staff Radar Antenna Design Engineer to lead the architecture, design, and production maturation of advanced waveguide antennas for high-performance imaging radar systems. This role is for a technical leader with deep expertise in electromagnetic design who can translate demanding radar performance requirements into robust, manufacturable antenna solutions. You will own antenna design from concept through vehicle integration, working across radar architecture, RF hardware, mechanical engineering, signal processing, manufacturing, validation, and suppliers. The ideal candidate combines first-principles electromagnetic insight with strong judgment in system tradeoffs, design-for-manufacturing, and execution of complex hardware programs. Responsibilities Define antenna architectures and performance targets for next-generation imaging radar systems, including field of view, angular resolution, gain, sidelobe levels, polarization, efficiency, bandwidth, scan performance, and calibration stability. Lead the design and optimization of advanced waveguide antenna technologies, including slotted-waveguide arrays, waveguide feeds, corporate and series-fed networks, apertures, transitions, radomes, and RF packaging interfaces. Develop electromagnetic models and design methods for complex antenna structures, accounting for mutual coupling, fabrication tolerances, thermal effects, dielectric loading, surface roughness, leakage, losses, and integration constraints. Drive antenna concepts through electromagnetic simulation, prototype design, fabrication, near-field and far-field measurement, correlation, root-cause analysis, and design iteration. Establish antenna-level budgets, verification plans, acceptance criteria, and correlation methodologies aligned with radar system performance. Partner with radar architects and RF engineers to optimize antenna, transceiver, packaging, calibration, and signal-processing tradeoffs at the system level. Lead integration of the antenna into automotive packaging, including radome effects, bumper and fascia materials, mounting constraints, environmental sealing, thermal management, and vehicle-level electromagnetic compatibility. The Lean Engineer III leads continuous improvement initiatives within assigned value streams to improve process capability, productivity, quality, flow, and operational performance. While applying Lean manufacturing principles, Six Sigma methodologies, and data-driven problem solving, this role analyzes and improves production systems, eliminates waste and variability, and implements sustainable process improvements that support business and manufacturing objectives.
The Lean Engineer III works cross-functionally with operations and functional teams, leads high-impact improvement projects, establishes effective production and problem-solving standards, and builds team capability through coaching and application of continuous improvement practices. This role uses strong analytical, technical, and influencing skills to identify improvement opportunities, facilitate problem solving, and sustain measurable results across manufacturing operations.
Key Responsibilities:
Lean & Six Sigma Improvement Execution: Lead and execute Lean and Six Sigma initiatives within assigned value streams, applying continuous improvement methodologies to improve productivity, quality, process capability, flow, and waste reduction in alignment with operational and business objectives.
Project Leadership & Delivery: Lead cross-functional improvement projects of moderate to high complexity, establishing objectives, coordinating activities, managing implementation, and ensuring measurable improvements are integrated into standard work and sustained over time.
Process Improvement & Problem Solving: Evaluate manufacturing and support processes to identify waste, variation, bottlenecks, and performance gaps; apply structured problem-solving methodologies to determine root causes and implement improvements in quality, cost, flow, and process capability.
Lean & Six Sigma Methodology Application: Apply appropriate Lean and Six Sigma methods, including DMAIC, Value Stream Mapping (VSM), Kaizen, 5S, Kanban, Standard Work, visual management, and Root Cause Analysis to improve process performance and operational effectiveness.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Influence:  Collaborate with Operations, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and other stakeholders to align improvement priorities, resolve barriers, coordinate implementation, and deliver sustainable results through effective influence without direct authority.
Continuous Improvement Capability Building: Coach project teams and operational stakeholders in structured problem solving and the effective application of Lean and Six Sigma methodologies to strengthen continuous improvement capabilities and reinforce process discipline.
Standardization & Governance: Support consistent application of Lean and Six Sigma methods, standards, and governance within assigned areas, ensuring improvement activities align with enterprise continuous improvement frameworks and local operating requirements.

Identify gaps in business metrics and then work with all levels of the factory value stream in establishing and executing a strategy for improving them

Document improvement process learning and shares best practices throughout the company
Identifies and brings forward to value stream team new project opportunities
Partners with the values stream Manager on strategic initiatives that strengthen standards compliance, accelerate the deployment of new systems, and shape innovative, future‑focused solutions that drive sustainable operational excellence across the value stream.

Other responsibilities as assigned

description:

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations.
